strengths: Addresses a practically important problem of MoE model deployment with comprehensive evaluation across 4 models and 7 benchmarks with detailed ablation studies
The dual-mask approach is intuitive and well-motivated for preserving both shared knowledge and expert specialization, with clear mathematical formulation
Strong results on specialized reasoning tasks (Table 4): retains 96.2% of Math-500 accuracy and 92% of AIME24 accuracy at 25% compression, significantly outperforming HC-SMoE

Achieves substantial compression efficiency: 45× faster compression than D2, enables single-GPU deployment from multi-GPU, and provides comprehensive ablation studies showing robustness to calibration dataset choice
Clever system co-design leveraging underutilized Bfloat16 exponent bits with verified zero perplexity degradation (Table 1) and custom CUDA kernel for efficient inference
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (saliency scoring from Wanda, element-wise masking from pruning literature, bit-packing from compression literature) without introducing fundamentally new methods

Inconsistent improvements across models: Mixtral shows 1.5% accuracy drop, DeepSeek 0.5% drop, Qwen1.5 0.5% drop, and Qwen3 1.4% drop at 50% compression compared to baselines, contradicting strong claims in abstract

Pairwise merging presented as a feature when it is actually a limitation imposed by the 3-bit packing constraint; k≥3 merging is computationally feasible (shown in Table 6) but algorithmically suboptimal, and this conflation is misleading

Expert grouping strategy appears suboptimal: search-based grouping achieves 0.3% higher accuracy (72.9% vs 72.6%) than default random grouping (Table 7), but is dismissed for 'simplicity' despite this non-negligible gap

Theoretical justification for similarity metric is weak: Appendix B.2 assumes independent normal distributions with σ₁ ≈ σ₂, which is violated in Mixtral-8x7B (correlation 0.2612, Table 9), yet the post-hoc analysis doesn't explain why the method still works
Missing critical analysis of failure modes: reasoning accuracy drops substantially on harder tasks (AIME25: ~11 points), but no investigation of which expert types fail or how to address this

Modest inference speedup (1.19-1.28×) that the paper acknowledges is 'marginally better' than existing methods; speedup source (model size vs. bit-packing scheme) is unclear and custom kernel contribution unquantified

Overstated claims: 'achieves up to 16.7% higher accuracy' cherry-picks the best model-method pair across different models; 'training-free' requires forward pass on calibration data; 'task-agnostic' still needs calibration

Bit-packing scheme robustness concerns: assumes narrow exponent range (112-128 in Bfloat16), may fail for future models or when combined with other compression techniques; no hardware portability analysis beyond A100
Missing ablations on reconstruction error, similarity metric alternatives, individual mask components (similarity-only vs. saliency-only), and calibration set size sensitivity

strengths: Strong practical contribution addressing real deployment challenges of MoE models with 50% compression while maintaining accuracy (0.2-1.4% drop across most models)

Comprehensive experimental validation across 4 diverse MoE models and 8 benchmarks with 6 strong baselines and thorough ablations

Missing generalizability analysis: no investigation of sensitivity to expert count/dimensions, routing policy changes post-compression, or performance on diverse model families

Comprehensive experimental evaluation with 16 random seeds, thorough ablation studies, and robustness demonstrations across calibration datasets and sparsity levels

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 4 MoE models and 9+ benchmarks with strong and consistent improvements over baselines (e.g., 16.7% higher MMLU accuracy at 50% compression vs HC-SMoE)

Practical and efficient: fast compression time (2 min vs 52 min for baselines), training-free, task-agnostic, and compatible with quantization

Excellent reproducibility: code promised, detailed algorithms, extensive ablations (calibration datasets, grouping strategies, similarity thresholds, higher sparsity levels), results averaged over 16 seeds with error reporting
System co-design with custom decode-GEMM kernel achieving ~2× throughput improvement and up to 1.80× end-to-end speedup through fused operations

Honest treatment of limitations and assumptions, with comprehensive supplementary analyses validating design choices (e.g., Gaussian weight distributions in A.5, exponent distribution across models in A.3)
weaknesses: Theoretical contributions are incremental: Lemma 3.1 applies standard probability theory to the problem; the Gaussian assumption is violated by Mixtral (correlation=0.26), causing noticeable deviation from theoretical predictions, and the independence assumption needed for derivation doesn't strictly hold

Pairwise merging restriction feels somewhat artificial—while exponential complexity argument for k≥3 is valid, Appendix A.8.4 acknowledges the merging algorithm itself can support arbitrary compression ratios with explicit mask storage, suggesting the constraint is a design choice rather than fundamental limitation
Bit-packing scheme is specific to BFloat16 format, limiting applicability as the field diversifies to other precision formats (FP8, QNF, etc.)

Search-based expert grouping strategy underexplored: random grouping is used as default despite being only ~0.3% worse than search-based alternatives (Table 5), without deep investigation of whether task-specific grouping could yield meaningful gains

Saliency metric choice lacks novelty: Appendix A.8.3 shows activation-based variants (WA, WAG) perform nearly identically to weight-only variants, suggesting the specific saliency choice is not critical and the component is somewhat incremental

Inference speedup gains are primarily from custom kernel (fused memory access for two experts) rather than the merging strategy itself; speedup diminishes significantly at larger batch sizes (1.29× at 512/512 config), limiting real-world applicability at scale

Incomplete baseline comparisons: recent MoE-specific quantization methods (MXMoE, MOEQuant, MILO) mentioned in related work but not experimentally compared; Wanda baseline applied only to experts (per footnote 1), potentially disadvantaging the baseline relative to its original design
Small calibration dataset (128 samples × 2048 tokens) with only Dataset-robustness validation in Table 4; lacks evaluation on larger calibration sets to strengthen generalization claims
Individual technical contributions feel more engineering-focused than conceptually novel (straightforward similarity identification, borrowed saliency masking from Wanda, bit-packing optimization)
